blocks.content:
Practice advanced PromQL in Explore: aggregate and join series, compare time windows, analyze distributions, and evaluate recording-rule and alert expressions. Work through one lesson at a time.

You need a working Prometheus data source and basic PromQL knowledge; [Prometheus + Grafana 101](bundled:prometheus-grafana-101) covers the basics. Use one Explore pane with query **A** expanded. These steps replace query A, so preserve any query you want to keep first.

**Customize for your data:** after choosing a source, use **Customize with Assistant** on each query to adapt metrics and labels before **Do it**. Review the suggestion, insert it, then run it. **Revert to original** restores the example. If Assistant is unavailable, edit the example yourself. Example metrics are not guaranteed to exist on your source.

Use a recent time range. Historical comparisons need older samples. If you see **No data**, check metric names, labels, and history; do not treat an empty result as proof that the system is healthy.

blocks.prompt: Choose the Prometheus data source to use in Explore.

blocks.content: Select **{{prometheusSource}}** in Explore.
blocks.tooltip: Use the Prometheus source you chose above.
Code mode lets you enter a PromQL expression directly.
blocks.content: Switch query **A** to **Code** mode to enter PromQL directly.
Start with a counter. Apply `rate()` before aggregating so counter resets are handled for each series.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
sum by (job, instance, handler) (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m]))
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect requests per second for each job, instance, and handler. `by` keeps only the labels you name.
Rank the aggregated request rates with `topk`.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
topk(5, sum by (handler) (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m])))
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect up to five handlers at each evaluation time. A range graph can show more than five distinct handlers as the ranking changes.
Compare `without` with `by`: exclude selected labels instead of naming every label to keep.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
sum without (instance) (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m]))
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

The instance label disappears, but every other label remains. Different status codes or handlers still produce separate series.
Use `=~` to include label values and `!~` to exclude them. Prometheus matches the whole label value.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
prometheus_http_requests_total{code=~"5..", handler!~"/|/-/.*"}
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect counters for 5xx responses outside the root and health endpoints. No matching series can mean no such errors were recorded; it does not prove the metric exists.
Enrich a rate with build metadata from the same monitored target. Ask Assistant to preserve a unique right-hand series for each matching label set.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m]) * on (job, instance) group_left (version) prometheus_build_info
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

The result retains request labels and gains `version`. The build-info value is 1, so the rate is unchanged. Missing matches drop out; multiple right-hand matches cause a cardinality error. Include cluster or namespace in `on` when job and instance are not unique.
A subquery evaluates an expression repeatedly: `[1h:1m]` samples the five-minute CPU rate once a minute over an hour.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
max_over_time(rate(process_cpu_seconds_total[5m])[1h:1m])
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect the largest sampled CPU rate for each process, measured in CPU-seconds per second. It is not a percentage. Recent processes have a shorter available history.
Gauges can rise and fall. Use `deriv` to fit a trend rather than treating decreases as counter resets.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
deriv(process_resident_memory_bytes[5m])
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect a slope in bytes per second: positive means rising memory, negative means falling memory. At least two samples are needed.
Use `offset` to compare matching series at different times. This example excludes zero historical rates before dividing.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
100 * (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m]) - rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m] offset 1h)) / (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m] offset 1h) > 0)
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Positive values mean an increase and negative values a decrease. Missing historical samples or a zero baseline produce no result, not a zero-percent change.
Aggregate both sides to the same labels before division. Define which response codes count as failures for your service.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
100 * sum by (job) (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / (sum by (job) (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m])) > 0)
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect the percentage of requests returning 5xx for each job with traffic. A missing error series is not automatically zero; verify instrumentation before adding a zero fallback. Zero-traffic jobs are excluded.
Use compatible gauges with the same labels and units. This example uses Node Exporter host memory, not a process virtual-address limit.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
100 * (1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / (node_memory_MemTotal_bytes > 0))
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect the percentage of host memory that is not available. Assistant can adapt this to another genuine used/capacity pair. Check label matching and capacity meaning before interpreting a ratio.
Use a classic request-duration histogram for a p95 estimate. Keep `le` when aggregating its buckets.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, job) (rate(prometheus_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect estimated p95 request duration in seconds per job. A summary such as `go_gc_duration_seconds` does not imply `_bucket` series exist. Native histograms use a different form without `le`; ask Assistant to match the metric type.
Divide the rate of total observed duration by the rate of observations. Aggregate both sides using the same labels.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
sum by (job) (rate(prometheus_http_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / (sum by (job) (rate(prometheus_http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) > 0)
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect mean request duration in seconds. This uses `_sum` and `_count`, not bucket boundaries, and also works for summaries of nonnegative observations. Zero-observation jobs are excluded; do not average precomputed summary quantiles.
Project a gauge four hours ahead using a linear fit over the last hour.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
predict_linear(process_resident_memory_bytes[1h], 4 * 3600)
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect predicted bytes, not certainty or time until exhaustion. Restarts, cycles, and workload changes can invalidate the trend; negative predictions are mathematically possible.
Compare the current rate with a rolling mean and standard deviation. This comparison filters series; it does not return a 0/1 score.

blocks.title: Compare a rate with its baseline

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
abs(rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m]) - avg_over_time(rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m])[1h:5m])) > (2 * stddev_over_time(rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m])[1h:5m]))
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Only series exceeding the threshold remain, carrying their absolute deviation. An empty result can be expected. Two standard deviations is a heuristic, not a guaranteed anomaly detector; seasonality and sparse traffic matter.
Evaluate the five-minute rate once per minute, then average those samples across 30 minutes.

blocks.title: Smooth a rate with a subquery

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
avg_over_time(rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m])[30m:1m])
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect a smoother rate in requests per second. Smaller subquery steps increase work; choose a resolution that answers your question.
A recording rule stores an expression for reuse. Here, success means a 2xx response; adapt that definition to your service before using it as an SLI.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
sum by (job) (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total{code=~"2.."}[5m])) / (sum by (job) (rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[5m])) > 0)
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect a success ratio from 0 to 1 where successful-request series and traffic exist. Missing series need investigation. This only evaluates the expression in Explore; it does not create a recording rule or an SLO.
Detect a missing series using a job you actually expect to be scraped. Customize the job before interpreting this result.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
absent(up{job="prometheus"})
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

A value of 1 means no matching series exists; an empty result means at least one exists, even if its `up` value is 0. Use `up == 0` for failed scrapes. This does not create an alert; a real rule also needs an evaluation and pending-period policy.
Grafana expands `$__rate_interval` using the query interval and configured scrape interval. It helps avoid windows too short to calculate a rate reliably.

blocks.tooltip: This is query A. Inserting a lesson replaces its current expression.
blocks.content:
Customize this example for your data, then replace query **A**:

```promql
rate(prometheus_http_requests_total[$__rate_interval])
```

blocks.tooltip: Run the expression, then compare the result with the lesson.
blocks.content:
Run the query and inspect the result.

Expect requests per second with a window that adapts to the time range. Keep scrape settings accurate, narrow label selectors, and limit unnecessary series. Reuse expensive frequent expressions through recording rules after validating them.

You have practiced aggregation, label filtering and joins, time comparisons, ratios, distributions, gauge trends, subqueries, and expressions suitable for recording and alerting rules.

Choose a pattern that answers a real question about your service. Check its metric types, units, labels, and missing-data behavior before reusing it in a dashboard or rule. See the [PromQL functions](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/functions/) and [vector matching](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/operators/#vector-matching) references for details.
